content.overview: Section 245 allows such number of member(s), depositor(s), or any class of them, as the Central Government may prescribe, to file an application before the Tribunal on behalf of the members or depositors, if they are of the opinion that the management or conduct of the affairs of the company are being conducted in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members or depositors. The Tribunal may restrain ultra vires, fraudulent or wrongful acts, restrain breach of provisions or of any agreement with members/depositors, declare a resolution void if passed by suppression of material facts or misstatement, restrain auditors or experts from acting, and claim damages or compensation from the company, directors, auditors, experts or advisors. An order binds all members or depositors of the class. The section is distinct from oppression under ss. 241–242 and from a common-law derivative action.
content.glance: Prescribed number of members or depositors may file class action; restrain ultra vires/fraud/wrongful acts and breaches; void resolutions obtained by suppression/misstatement; claim damages from company, directors, auditors, experts; order binds the class; distinct from oppression and derivative suits.
content.study: Such number of member(s), depositor(s), or any class of them, as the Central Government may prescribe, may file an application before the Tribunal on behalf of the members or depositors, if they are of the opinion that the management or conduct of the affairs of the company are being conducted in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members or depositors. The Tribunal may, among other things, restrain the company from committing an act which is ultra vires, restrain breach of any provision of the Act or of any agreement with members or depositors, declare a resolution altering the memorandum or articles void if passed by suppression of material facts or misstatement, restrain auditors or experts, and claim damages or compensation from the company or from any director, auditor, expert, advisor or consultant for any fraudulent, unlawful or wrongful act. Current-law framing: confirm prescribed threshold of members or depositors; identify prejudice to company, members or depositors; map the relief sought to the list in the section; note that the order binds the class. Distinguish ss. 241–242 (oppression/mismanagement with different standing and remedial focus) and common-law derivative actions.

sections.heading: Standing
sections.body: Prescribed number of members, depositors, or any class of them may apply on behalf of the members or depositors.

sections.heading: Ground
sections.body: Management or conduct of affairs conducted in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members or depositors.

sections.heading: Reliefs
sections.body: Restrain ultra vires, fraudulent or wrongful acts and breaches; void resolutions obtained by suppression or misstatement; restrain auditors/experts; claim damages from company, directors, auditors, experts or advisors.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Order binds all members or depositors of the class; distinct from s. 241 oppression and from derivative action.

examples.title: Depositors' class action
examples.body: A prescribed number of depositors apply under s. 245 alleging that the company's affairs are conducted prejudicially to depositors and seeking damages from directors and the auditor for wrongful acts. The application is maintainable if the threshold and grounds are met.

examples.title: Distinct from oppression
examples.body: A single member with standing under s. 244 seeks oppression relief under s. 241. That is not a class action under s. 245; the two routes have different thresholds, applicants (members vs members/depositors) and relief catalogues.

hypotheticals.question: Is every member automatically able to file a class action under s. 245?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 245 requires such number of members or depositors as the Central Government may prescribe. The prescribed threshold must be met; it is not open to every individual member as of right.

distinctions.title: Class action (s. 245) vs oppression (ss. 241–242)
distinctions.left: Prescribed class of members or depositors; restraint and damages against company, directors, auditors, experts
distinctions.right: s. 244 standing members; end the matters complained of by regulating conduct, share purchase, etc.

misconceptions.trap: Class action under s. 245 is the same as an oppression petition under s. 241.
misconceptions.correction: Standing, applicants (including depositors), and the catalogue of reliefs differ. Section 245 is a separate statutory class-action route.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 245 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm prescribed threshold of members/depositors. II. Test prejudice ground. III. Map reliefs sought. IV. Distinguish oppression. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Class composition; prejudice facts; reliefs; precise order sought.

examTips: Prescribed number of members or depositors.
Prejudice to company, members or depositors.
Order binds the class; distinct from oppression.

learningObjectives: State who may bring a class action under s. 245 and what reliefs are available.
Distinguish class action from oppression under ss. 241–242.
enhancement.definition: Section 245 allows a prescribed number of members or depositors to apply to the Tribunal on behalf of the class where the company's affairs are conducted prejudicially to the company, members or depositors, with powers to restrain wrongful acts and claim damages from the company, directors, auditors and experts.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Collective member and depositor harm can be redressed by a statutory class action that binds the class and reaches professionals as well as the company and directors.
essentialIngredients: Prescribed number of members or depositors
Affairs conducted prejudicially to company, members or depositors
Reliefs: restraint, voidance of tainted resolutions, damages from company/directors/auditors/experts
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 245 is the statutory class-action provision for members and depositors.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm threshold; test prejudice; map reliefs; distinguish oppression.

verification.note: Section-text level; prescribed numbers depend on rules; case-law verification separate; no new citations invented.
